title: Hare traction splint
stem: Trauma room. Mr Lo, 30, about 65 kg, came off his motorbike. He has an isolated closed mid-shaft fracture of the left femur (confirmed on X-ray): the thigh is swollen, shortened and deformed. He is haemodynamically stable. Nurse Tung is with you. Apply a Hare traction splint, explaining as you go.

phases.title: Prepare him
phases.goal: Monitoring, explain and consent, and analgesia from the cart before you touch the leg.

phases.title: The splint
phases.goal: By hand: check the leg and foot, measure, straps, hitch, traction, ring, wind, secure, check again.

notes:
Checked against manufacturer guidance for the Hare traction splint, JRCALC, and BOAST guidance on femoral shaft fractures.

Indication: isolated closed mid-shaft femoral fracture — traction reduces pain, muscle spasm and bleeding, and improves alignment. Contraindications: pelvic fracture, hip injury, knee injury or proximal tibial fracture, ankle or foot injury on the same leg, partial amputation, and (relative) open fracture with exposed bone ends. Give analgesia first (IV opioid and/or a femoral nerve or fascia iliaca block). Check pulses, motor and sensory function before and after.

Steps: measure against the uninjured leg (ischial tuberosity to about 20 cm beyond the heel); open and position the support straps; apply the ankle hitch; take manual traction; slide the splint under the leg with the ring against the ischial tuberosity; secure the ischial strap; attach the hitch to the traction hook; wind the ratchet to mechanical traction (about 10% of body weight, up to 7 kg / 15 lb, or until pain eases and the leg length is similar); release manual traction; fasten the leg straps (avoiding the knee and fracture); raise the stand; re-check neurovascular status.

Your notes match this, including the 10% body weight up to 7 kg guide.

Perfect script checked against the Hare manufacturer's guidance and PHTLS, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. The flow you reviewed is kept; wrong options removed and one analgesic scored, so the guide asks for one.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

steps.label: Explain
steps.hint: What the splint does, analgesia first, and his consent.

opts.t: Mr Lo, your thigh bone is broken. I'll give you strong painkiller first, then put on a splint that gently pulls the leg straight. That eases the pain and the bleeding. Is that OK?
opts.tz: 盧生，你條大髀骨斷咗。我會先俾強力止痛藥你，跟住幫你戴一個牽引夾板，慢慢將條腳拉直，咁樣會冇咁痛，亦會少啲出血。可唔可以？
opts.r: Mr Lo: "Yes… anything to stop this pain."

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Analgesia before anyone touches the leg: an IV opioid now; a block can follow.

opts.t: Levobupivacaine 0.25% 30 mL (75 mg) for an ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block
opts.dose: 30 mL (75 mg) for an ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block
opts.r: Good, but it takes 15–20 minutes to work: give an IV opioid now as well.
opts.mark: Adds a fascia iliaca block for ongoing analgesia

steps.label: Apply the Hare splint
steps.hint: Expose and check the foot, measure on the good leg, straps, ankle hitch, manual traction, ring to the ischium, wind, secure, re-check.

opts.performHint: Do every step with your hands. Mr Lo, his leg and his foot respond to what you do.
mark: Sizes the splint on the uninjured leg
Correct position against the ischial tuberosity
Mechanical traction to the correct amount

qs.q: Main indication for a Hare splint?

qs.a: About 10% of body weight, up to 7 kg
wrong: About 50% of body weight, up to 30 kg
Just enough to take up slack

qs.q: Blood loss from a closed femoral shaft fracture?

qs.a: Reduces pain, spasm and bleeding; restores length

rules.fail: The splint went on before any analgesia.

badge.name: Pull Straight
badge.flavor: Analgesia, hitch, ring on the ischium, 10% traction, check again.

cards.why: Pressure on the ischium worsens pelvic injury.

cards.q: The Hare splint ring sits against…

options: IV opioid and/or a femoral nerve block
None; the traction itself is the analgesia
Local infiltration at the fracture site

cards.q: Femoral shaft fracture blood loss can reach…

options: Remove the ankle hitch after 10 minutes
Apply ice to the groin strap

cards.q: Nerve at risk from a tight strap near the fibular head?

script.say: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2.
Mr Lo, your thigh bone is broken. I'll give you strong painkiller first, then put on a splint that gently pulls the leg straight. That eases the pain and the bleeding. Is that OK?
script.do: Mr Lo: "Yes… anything to stop this pain."

script.say: Fentanyl 1 microgram/kg (65 microgram) IV, titrated. Levobupivacaine 0.25% 30 mL (75 mg) for an ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block.
script.do: Good, but it takes 15–20 minutes to work: give an IV opioid now as well.

script.say: Check the foot first: pulses, sensation and movement. No pelvic, hip, knee or ankle injury on this side. Measure on the good leg, ischial tuberosity to 20 cm beyond the heel. Straps opened and placed. Ankle hitch on. Nurse Tung holds manual traction; the splint slides under, the ring against the ischial tuberosity; ischial strap done. Hitch to the hook, wind to about 10% of body weight, 6 to 7 kg, until the pain eases. Leg straps, avoiding the knee and the fracture. Stand up. Then the foot again: pulses, sensation and movement.
